issue_context.title: [homematic] - GAS_POWER is using an invalid state_class (measurement)
issue_context.body:
### The problem

**The issue:**
The homematic integration is using a wrong state_class for the Sensor `GAS_POWER`

Log:
```
Entity sensor.seq3475587_gas_power (<class 'homeassistant.components.homematic.sensor.HMSensor'>)
is using state class 'measurement' which is impossible considering device class ('gas')
it is using; expected None or one of 'total_increasing', 'total';
Please update your configuration if your entity is manually configured, otherwise create a bug report at
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22integration%3A+homematic%22


Entity sensor.ueq1258992_gas_power (<class 'homeassistant.components.homematic.sensor.HMSensor'>)
is using state class 'measurement' which is impossible considering device class ('gas') it is using;
expected None or one of 'total_increasing', 'total';
Please update your configuration if your entity is manually configured, otherwise create a bug report at
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22integration%3A+homematic%22
```

The specific area in the code is this in the sensor.py:
```
    "GAS_POWER": SensorEntityDescription(
        key="GAS_POWER",
        native_unit_of_measurement=UnitOfVolume.CUBIC_METERS,
        device_class=SensorDeviceClass.GAS,
        state_class=SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT,
    ),
    "GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER": SensorEntityDescription(
        key="GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER",
        native_unit_of_measurement=UnitOfVolume.CUBIC_METERS,
        device_class=SensorDeviceClass.GAS,
        state_class=SensorStateClass.TOTAL_INCREASING,
    ),
```

Since GAS_POWER is no TOTAL_INCREASING nor an TOTAL measurement state_class, NONE should probably be the correct option.


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2024.7.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

homematic

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homematic

review_comments:
Hmm I feel like this unit of measurement is wrong in that case?

What does this unit represent?

../Frenck

hi :)
tbh - this is probably a bit more complex than i thought...

there are several issues:

1. The device is no longer available
2. The documentation which I found does only mention m³ per impulse

I don't have a GAS sensor, since I don't have GAS at all... I just have the same device, to which different sensors can be configured (Gas, Electicity, etc.)
On my production System, I am using a custom_component for Homematic - on another test-system, I have installed the core integration - and here, I do get the warning in the logs...
(since I don't have the GAS sensor, it won't be initialized at all - the core integration does.

Therefore, I've searched the custom_component, how it has been integrated here... 
And it seems, that it is in exact the same way as with this integration:


```
    "GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER": HmSensorEntityDescription(
        key="GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER",
        native_unit_of_measurement=UnitOfVolume.CUBIC_METERS,
        device_class=SensorDeviceClass.GAS,
        state_class=SensorStateClass.TOTAL_INCREASING,
    ),
```

```
    "GAS_POWER": HmSensorEntityDescription(
        key="GAS_POWER",
        native_unit_of_measurement=UnitOfVolume.CUBIC_METERS,
        state_class=SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT,
    ),
``` 

there are also some other sensors, but these are probably from the newer HomematicIP GAS Sensor...
```
    "GAS_FLOW": HmSensorEntityDescription(
        key="GAS_FLOW",
        native_unit_of_measurement=UnitOfVolumeFlowRate.CUBIC_METERS_PER_HOUR,
        device_class=SensorDeviceClass.VOLUME_FLOW_RATE,
        state_class=SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT,
    ), 
    "GAS_VOLUME": HmSensorEntityDescription(
        key="GAS_VOLUME",
        native_unit_of_measurement=UnitOfVolume.CUBIC_METERS,
        device_class=SensorDeviceClass.GAS,
        state_class=SensorStateClass.TOTAL_INCREASING,
    ),
```

At least, it seems, that GAS_POWER does provide the cubic_meters per impule, while GAS_ENERGY_COUNTER seems to be a total_increasing value.
![grafik](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/26391061/14ccf1b3-d701-401b-9ca0-3e6a486a45c8)

So "measurement" would be correct - in my opinion - the other way would be to support this for m³ at all...

> that GAS_POWER does provide the cubic_meters per impule

> So "measurement" would be correct - in my opinion - the other way would be to support this for m³ at all...

I don't agree, I think the unit of measurement is incorrect. As this is not just m³, but it is a usage over time, a flow rate, meaning I would expect it to have a timeframe attached to it. E.g., m³/min or something like that (whatever an impulse is).

So this probably should have been using a flow rate unit (`UnitOfVolumeFlowRate`), which would accept an `measurement` state class.

ok, I was not sure, if I should change the unit - since I could not test it by myself (since I do not have the device)...

From the HomematicIP-Cloud integration, this seems to be the FlowRate - but I think, the timeframe of the impulse could be different from meter to meter...

If you want, I can delete the PR and keep this as it is for now... 
And I can MAYBE ask in the forum of the custom component how they have implemented this and what they think (since the developer of the custom component was one of the code owners of this one for some time)

> If you want, I can delete the PR and keep this as it is for now...

I think this PR is valid, I just opened up the discussion to see if we could adjust the unit of measurement instead. But if we don't know... we don't know :)

Let's keep the PR as is and resolve the error message.

thanks for the merge - I was just about to write, that I would put the PR back to draft, until I have more information.

The chance is pretty low, that someone will probably hit this bug - many users have changed to the custom_component (afaik) - and there, it still seems to be a measurement sensor ^^
Also, since the Hardware is quite old, there is a chance, that people are either using the homematicip_cloud integration, where the gas sensor has been implemented with the 2024.7. release - or, they are trying to implement this on their homematic CCU (where the newer sensor is probably not implemented at all)

Well, we would be open to improve the built-in integration 🙏 

../Frenck
